title: Very small employers carry a high per-employee payroll tax reporting burden by IRS estimate

history.reason: IRS burden examples read directly; scaling per W-2 recorded.

description: The IRS estimates employment tax reporting burden is far higher per employee for small employers (15.9 hours and $620 per Form W-2 in its four-W-2 example) than for large employers (0.4 hours and $20 per W-2).
customer_segment: Employers with few employees filing the Form 941 series and wage statements.
context: IRS model-based estimates as of October 1, 2025 law; whether small employers actually spend this time given payroll services is unknown.

evidence.text: IRS estimates an employer issuing four Forms W-2 has an average burden of 63.6 hours and $2,480, versus 800 hours and $40,000 for 2,000 W-2s.
IRS states most employers experience lower than average burden and that the figures are national averages.
Many small employers may offload this work to payroll providers, shrinking their own time but paying fees.

alternatives: Payroll software and outsourced payroll/accounting services: adoption not investigated.

contradictory_evidence.text: The IRS says most employers experience lower than average burden, so the examples may overstate typical small-employer time.
Established payroll providers may already solve this; the unmet need is unknown.

uncertainty: Unknown: real time spent by very small employers, share using payroll services, fees paid, and remaining pain.
open_questions: How do very small employers actually file, and what do they pay for it?
What gaps remain with existing payroll providers?
next_actions: Find independent survey data on small-employer payroll time and provider usage.
